SiC and GaNs are the best choices for the next-generation inverters.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GaN is the best choice for single-phase inverters in terms of switching loss reduction, heat sink volume reduction, output filter volume reduction, and dead-time reduction.
GaN HEMT has better efficiency and switching performance than Si IGBT and SiC MOSFETS at high frequency.
GaN has better performance than SiC and Si in T-type inverter applications, and GaN-based inverters can be operated at high frequency with low losses and low harmonic distortion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GaN HEMT-based converters have better efficiency, smaller heat sink and filter volumes than Si IGBT- and SiC MOSFETS-based converters at high-frequency operation.
GaN-based inverters can operate at 160 kHz with 97% efficiency at 3-kW output power with a 3.5 $^{\circ }\text{C}$ increase in case temperature and 1.5 W increase in power losses.
GaN-based converters can be used in a wide range of applications, from low to high power, from low to medium temperature, and from low to high switching frequency.
